correctness.rationale: For arbitrary real exceptional resistance x>0 and all integers n>=3, the proof constructs the inverse grounded-path diagonal s(T-s)/T, derives the exact cycle-pair formula by finite sums, optimizes all positions at fixed separation via AB, and treats the strong-link integer separation by explicit strictly positive second derivative and signed neighboring differences. The weak-link solution is a complete finite argmin formula that includes every tie. All cases n=3, x=1 and adjacent leaders are included. A separately written exact matrix inversion routine reproduced 1476 pair values and all candidate sets in 72 rational instances. Finite checks are not substituted for the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The newly stated structural result is an explicit all-finite-resistance one-edge-defect location classification, with a strong-link endpoint theorem and a weak-link O(n) scalar minimization. Fitch and Leonard solve unweighted cycle and path endpoint models; Patterson, McGlohon, and Dyagilev solve arbitrary weighted cycles through general weighted-digraph dynamic programming. The general algorithm is covering as a numerical decision procedure, but its theorems do not state the defect-relative location transition or the analytic candidate collapse and do not immediately imply them without additional Green-kernel and optimization arguments. Targeted mathematical literature and published-results comparisons did not reveal a dominating explicit statement. Residual specialized priority risk is acknowledged.
residual_risks: A specialized source on single-defect leader placement, if not indexed or inspected, could state an equivalent closed phase classification.
The general weighted-ring algorithm formally computes the finite-weight answer; it is explicitly acknowledged as broader numerical coverage, not presented as absence of preceding solvability.
No independent specialist review has determined historical priority.

value.rationale: A single weak or strengthened link is a natural structured communication failure/reinforcement problem. The all-n/all-positive-x optimum gives a sharp, counterintuitive switch between endpoint-anchored and centered leader placement; an exact O(n) method for all weak-link parameter values and an explicit two-pair strong-link theorem. The two-leader design is operationally motivated by total noisy follower deviation, and the result interpolates between independently known equal-cycle and broken-path designs. This precise structural information is not supplied by finite experiments or a generic polynomial-time decision procedure.
